name: Austria
tagline: Your IB Diploma is enough on paper - but almost everything is in German
summary: Austria is unusually simple on recognition: a properly acquired IB Diploma counts as a full Austrian university entrance qualification by law, with no points table and no subject-combination rule to satisfy. The catch is language. Public universities teach bachelor's degrees in German and expect you to prove it, so an IB student without solid German is pushed towards a handful of private universities and Fachhochschulen. For EU students the money side is easy: you pay about 26 EUR a semester in student union fees for the first few years and nothing else.
whyConsider: The IB Diploma is explicitly named by the ministry as satisfying the general university entrance qualification - no equivalence procedure, no nostrification.
EU/EEA students pay no tuition during the normal length of the degree plus two tolerance semesters; the only compulsory payment is the OeH fee of 26.20 EUR per semester.
No entrance exam for most subjects - if you have the Diploma and the German, you enrol.
Vienna is consistently ranked among the most liveable cities in Europe and student transport and culture are heavily discounted.
Deadlines are late by European standards: the general admission period for the winter semester runs into early September, which fits an IB student with July results.
watchOuts: German is the real barrier. Austrian universities expect proof of German, typically a school certificate showing at least four years of German lessons or a recognised language diploma.
English-taught bachelor's at public universities are scarce. The English-taught options are mostly private universities and Fachhochschulen, which charge real fees.
Popular subjects are access-regulated (zugangsgeregelt) and have their own registration windows that close months before the general deadline - often in spring, before your results exist.
Medicine is the extreme case: the MedAT registration window closed on 31 March 2026 for a test on 8 July 2026, so you must register long before IB results day.
Once you pass the standard study duration plus two tolerance semesters, the 363.36 EUR per semester tuition fee starts, so a slow degree costs money.

ibRecognition.minimumPoints: A properly acquired IB Diploma. The Austrian ministry names the IB Diploma as satisfying the general university entrance qualification without further procedure; no separate Austrian points threshold above the IB's own pass standard (24 points and the IB's pass conditions) was found published.
ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: None published. Unlike Germany and Switzerland, Austria does not impose an IB subject-combination rule for general university entrance. What can be imposed is a subject-specific requirement for an individual degree (besondere Universitaetsreife), for example a supplementary examination in Latin or in a particular subject - this is set by the individual university's curriculum, not centrally.
notes: The legal position (bmfwf.gv.at): a foreign certificate gives general university entrance either (a) because the university finds it opens higher education in the issuing country and shows no substantial difference from an Austrian Reifepruefungszeugnis, or (b) because it is one of the named certificates - which explicitly include a properly acquired IB Diploma and the European Baccalaureate - or (c) through at least three years of completed higher education elsewhere.
The admitting university's Studienabteilung makes the decision. There is no central Austrian recognition authority for school-leaving certificates.

No official IB-points-to-Austrian-grade conversion table was found. Austrian admission is normally pass/fail against the qualification rather than ranked by grade, except where an entrance procedure applies.

Admission to a specific degree can still depend on extra prerequisites - language proof, or a supplementary examination (Ergaenzungspruefung) in a subject the curriculum requires. Check the curriculum of the exact degree, and get this confirmed by the university in writing; this research could not verify the current Latin/Biology/Maths supplementary rules from an official page.

portal.name: Each university's own application portal; study search via studienwahl.at

deadlines.label: General admission period for the winter semester, EU/EEA/Swiss applicants (University of Vienna)
deadlines.notes: The 5 September cut-off is the standard Austrian winter-semester deadline and is comfortably after IB results day. Re-check the exact 2027 dates from spring 2027; other universities publish their own but usually land on the same date.

deadlines.label: General admission period for the winter semester, third-country nationals (University of Vienna)
deadlines.notes: If you are not an EU/EEA/Swiss citizen, the window closes about a month earlier and you also need a residence permit, which takes months.

deadlines.label: Degrees with an entrance procedure (Aufnahmeverfahren)
deadlines.date: Registration can close up to six months before the semester starts
deadlines.notes: Study in Austria states that programmes with entrance examinations have earlier deadlines, up to six months before the start of the semester. For a September 2027 start that can mean registering in spring 2027, before you have any IB results.

deadlines.label: MedAT - human and dental medicine entrance test
deadlines.notes: For 2026 entry, registration ran 2-31 March 2026 and the test was held on 8 July 2026 for 1,950 places across the four medical universities. Registration closes months before IB results, so decide early. Re-check medizinstudieren.at from January 2027.

deadlines.label: Summer semester intake
deadlines.notes: Not all degrees admit in the summer semester.

steps: From autumn 2026, pick the degree first and read its curriculum - that is where any subject prerequisite or supplementary examination is written down.
Check whether the degree is access-regulated. If it is, find the registration window now; it will close long before the general September deadline.
Sort out German. If the degree is German-taught you need documented German, and building that takes a year, not a month.
Register on the university's application portal when the admission period opens in June 2027 and upload your school documents.
Send your IB Diploma as soon as it arrives in early July 2027 and complete admission before 5 September 2027.
Pay the OeH fee, collect your student ID, and register your address (Meldezettel) and your EU registration certificate after you arrive.
application.selectionNotes: Most Austrian degrees are open: meet the entrance qualification and the language requirement and you are admitted. A defined list of subjects is access-regulated with a capped number of places and its own entrance procedure - medicine and dentistry through the MedAT, and a set of high-demand subjects such as psychology, business, computer science, biology, pharmacy and architecture at individual universities. The exact list and place numbers change, so verify per university for 2027/28.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: Limited. Austrian public universities teach bachelor's degrees overwhelmingly in German. English-taught bachelor's are concentrated in private universities (MODUL University Vienna, Webster Vienna, Lauder Business School) and universities of applied sciences (IMC Krems, MCI Innsbruck, FHWien der WKW), and a small number of public-university programmes. Do not assume a programme is in English - check the language of instruction field on studienwahl.at for each one.
language.englishProof: For English-taught programmes, IB English A is normally accepted and English B HL usually is; requirements are set per institution and were not verified centrally in this research.
notes: Study in Austria states that proof of German is mandatory for most programmes, and that acceptable proof includes a school leaving certificate confirming German lessons of at least four years, or a German language diploma.
Four years of German B in the IB may satisfy this, but get it confirmed in writing by the university before you rely on it.
If your German is not accepted, the route in is the Vorstudienlehrgang (university preparation programme), which adds time and cost.
Even at an English-taught private university, daily life in Vienna, Graz or Innsbruck runs in German.

tuitionEuEea.value: No tuition fee during the standard duration of the degree plus two tolerance semesters. After that it is 363.36 EUR per semester. You always pay the OeH student union fee of 26.20 EUR per semester.

tuitionNonEu.value: 726.72 EUR per semester from the first semester, plus the 26.20 EUR OeH fee, giving 752.92 EUR per semester. Some exemptions exist for students from certain countries and for scholarship holders.

livingCostMonthly.value: About 1,300 EUR per month: accommodation 450-700 EUR in a hall of residence, food around 300 EUR, and around 500 EUR for transport, study materials and everything else. Vienna is above the average, smaller cities below it.

notes: The official Study in Austria fees page still shows an older OeH figure of 25.20 EUR and a non-EU total of 751.92 EUR. The 26.20 EUR figure from the OeH itself and from the University of Vienna is the current one; the OeH fee is index-linked and announced each year by 1 May, so expect a small increase before 2027/28.
Fachhochschulen may charge tuition of their own - each one sets it, so check the individual school.
Private universities set their own fees and they are substantial. These were not verified from official pages in this research.

funding: Danish SU can in many cases be taken abroad for a full degree - check with SU Styrelsen first, as this is usually the biggest single source of money.
OeAD administers Austrian scholarship schemes; the scholarship database at grants.at is the official place to search.
Individual universities and Fachhochschulen run their own merit and hardship funds - ask the student advisory service directly.
Erasmus+ applies once you are enrolled and want to spend a period in another country.
workRights: As a Danish (EU) citizen you have free access to the Austrian labour market with no permit and no hour cap; you are limited only by tax and social-insurance thresholds for marginal employment. Non-EU students need a work permit and are restricted in hours - the specific limit for bachelor students was not verified from an official page in this research, so check with the OeAD before relying on it.
residency: EU/EEA citizens staying longer than three months must obtain a Confirmation of Registration (Anmeldebescheinigung) for students, on top of the ordinary address registration (Meldezettel) that everyone in Austria completes after moving in. No visa or residence permit is needed. Non-EU students need a student residence permit applied for before travelling. Source: OeAD entry and residence pages.
housing: Student halls are run by providers such as OeAD Housing, OeJAB and Home4Students rather than by the universities themselves, and the good ones fill up over the summer - apply as soon as you decide on a city. Vienna has the largest supply but also the most competition in September; Graz, Innsbruck, Linz and Salzburg are easier. Private shared flats are the fallback and are advertised in German.
healthcare: Health insurance is compulsory. With a Danish EHIC you are covered for necessary treatment, but for a full degree you will normally want proper Austrian cover: students who are not covered through a parent or a job can take out student self-insurance with the OeGK. Register with an Austrian insurer soon after arriving and carry your e-card. The current student self-insurance premium was not verified from an official page in this research - check oegk.at.

institutions.name: University of Vienna
institutions.note: The oldest university in the German-speaking world and by far Austria's largest; bachelor's teaching is in German, and several popular subjects are access-regulated.

institutions.name: TU Wien
institutions.note: Austria's main technical university, in the middle of Vienna; bachelor's are German-taught, with English arriving at master's level.

institutions.name: Vienna University of Economics and Business
institutions.note: One of Europe's biggest business schools, on a striking modern campus by the Prater; business bachelor's entry is regulated and competitive.

institutions.name: University of Graz
institutions.note: Austria's second-oldest university in a UNESCO-listed student city that is cheaper and calmer than Vienna.

institutions.name: Graz University of Technology
institutions.note: Strong engineering school with deep links to the Styrian automotive and semiconductor industry.

institutions.name: University of Innsbruck
institutions.note: World-class quantum physics group and a campus surrounded by the Alps; the obvious pick if mountains matter to you.

institutions.name: Johannes Kepler University Linz
institutions.note: Modern campus university with an unusually strong machine-learning group; check the language of instruction for its AI and computer science degrees, as some are taught in English.

institutions.name: University of Salzburg
institutions.note: Mid-sized university in a small, expensive, very beautiful city an hour from Munich.

institutions.name: University of Klagenfurt
institutions.note: Small campus university by a lake in Carinthia, with a noticeably high international share for its size.

institutions.name: BOKU University
institutions.note: Austria's university of natural resources and life sciences - the place for environment, agriculture and water engineering.

institutions.name: Medical University of Vienna
institutions.note: Entry is only through the MedAT test, which you register for in March - long before IB results - and the degree is taught in German.

institutions.name: MODUL University Vienna
institutions.englishBachelors: English-taught bachelor's in tourism, hospitality, management and new media - verify the current list and the fee directly.
institutions.note: Private university on the Kahlenberg above Vienna, teaching entirely in English; fees were not verified from an official page in this research.

institutions.name: Webster Vienna Private University
institutions.englishBachelors: English-taught American-style bachelor's, mainly in business, psychology and international relations - verify the current list and the fee directly.
institutions.note: The Vienna campus of an American university, so the degree structure and credits are US-style; fees were not verified from an official page in this research.

institutions.name: IMC Krems University of Applied Sciences
institutions.englishBachelors: Several bachelor's are taught in English, including business, health and life science subjects - verify the current list and the fee directly.
institutions.note: Applied-sciences school in a small Danube wine town an hour from Vienna, with compulsory internships built into the degree.

institutions.name: MCI - The Entrepreneurial School
institutions.englishBachelors: A number of bachelor's are taught in English, mostly in management and engineering - verify the current list and the fee directly.
institutions.note: Practice-oriented school in Innsbruck with a business-school feel and strong industry placements.
